name: Vellichor
description: Vellichor is a hippocampal retrograde activator that binds to memory-encoding SNT clusters, allowing the user to re-experience consolidated memories with full sensory fidelity — not as recollection, but as lived presence. The drug selectively amplifies emotional valence, meaning every recalled moment feels better than it did the first time.
effects: Full-immersion playback of chosen autobiographical memories
Profound sense of presence and temporal displacement
Warm euphoria during transition between memory states
side_effects: Severe anhedonia upon return to baseline — reality feels thin and colorless
Progressive inability to form new positive memories
Memory bleed — fragments of replayed memories intrude on waking life
Users with traumatic histories risk unintended trauma replay
Long-term: dissolution of the present-tense self
duration: 2-6 hours per session, depth scales with dose
cultural_context: Originally developed as palliative care therapy for the terminally ill — a way to die happy. It leaked into recreational markets within eighteen months. In Tier 3 and 4, Vellichor is the drug of the quietly desperate: people with good-enough pasts and unbearable presents. Support groups exist. They don't work well. The street name 'the Ache' refers not to the high but to what comes after.
story_hooks: A user contacts the party because their Vellichor sessions keep replaying a memory they swear they never lived — someone else's memory, bleeding through a corrupted SNT batch
A Helix executive is found catatonic, jacked into a Vellichor loop that won't release — someone has locked the exit pathway and is using her replaying memories to extract corporate intelligence
A character's loved one has stopped eating, stopped leaving their apartment; their Vellichor use has progressed to the point where the present holds nothing for them
